title: Abalone shell
author: Marcel Padilla

geometry.units: COLMAP reconstruction scale of the parent capture, not metric

capture.device: phone, handheld orbit, 4K/60 landscape, 202 frames used
capture.surface: speckle mat (texture for COLMAP feature matching)
capture.object_pose: suspended on a bottle stand, so the orbit sees the underside too

pipeline.training: Brush (built from main), 30000 iters, 500k splat cap
pipeline.frame: canonical (object at the origin, up = -Y, first video frame's viewpoint on +Z)

steps: cropped to the object alone, then recentred on its bounding box

caveats: Spherical harmonics were dropped (SH degree 0), so there is no view-dependent shading. That costs this object more than most: the nacre's iridescence IS view-dependent, so the colours are frozen at one viewing direction rather than shifting as you orbit.
Scale is the COLMAP reconstruction scale of the parent capture and is not metric.

A few residual gaussians float inside the concave side. 3D Gaussian splatting explains a specular concavity partly with floaters, and with SH dropped they stay as opaque flecks; the hand-crop removed the room but not these.
PSNR/SSIM are the parent capture's held-out evaluation at 30k iterations (abalone_shell2, 202/202 frames registered), not a measurement of this cropped file.
